- Europe/Central Asia: Public health guidance explicitly endorsed delivery-and-collect and home-based ART options to reduce travel for patients during COVID-19, with telehealth layered on to reduce in-person contacts, reflecting system-level acceptance across provider networks and payers.<cite id="ed98fdaa-7">Arrangements were made in some countries to administer antiretroviral therapy (ART) through delivery and collection services for those unable to travel or</cite> <cite id="0512daff-4">Implementing telemedicine allows for maintenance of social distancing and limits in-person interactions, necessary during the COVID-19 Pandemic</cite>

Quantitative and qualitative signals of acceptance and uptake
- Uptake data: Multi-country analyses during COVID-19 show that even amid general treatment disruptions, home delivery and MCD were among the most rapidly scaled interventions to prevent loss to follow-up, with reported reductions in interruption and retention maintained in many settings; for example, modeling and regional reports link acceptance of delivery-and-collect to tangible prevention of additional infections and deaths.<cite id="069ef15a-2">The cost of inaction: COVID-19-related service disruptions could cause hundreds of thousands of extra deaths from HIV. Gains made in preventing</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-7">Arrangements were made in some countries to administer antiretroviral therapy (ART) through delivery and collection services for those unable to travel or</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-8">About 16% of people living with HIV (PLWH) were unaware of their HIV status, 27% were unable to receive ART, and 34% of those who received ART</cite>
- Patient acceptance: Experiences from Southeast Asia document high patient acceptability and perceived convenience of home delivery due to reduced travel/clinic exposure and flexible dosing windows; peer-reviewed and NGO-supported programs in Côte d’Ivoire likewise report strong uptake and adherence support through telehealth coordination.<cite id="ed98fdaa-0">This report describes how HIV programs in Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, and Nigeria supported treatment continuation by introducing home delivery of ARVs</cite> <cite id="0512daff-5">Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, CCP is delivering antiretroviral medication directly to the homes of people living with HIV in Cote d'Ivoire</cite>

What this means for countries and regions
- Regions with widespread acceptance and implementation: Southeast Asia; parts of Europe/Central Asia; several West and Central African countries and networks; and select Western Pacific countries with strong NGO/bilateral support.<cite id="ed98fdaa-2">National programmes in 8 out of 10 countries in the region have issued guidelines for MMD of ARV drugs and take-away doses of OST drugs, beefing up their ARV</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-7">Arrangements were made in some countries to administer antiretroviral therapy (ART) through delivery and collection services for those unable to travel or</cite> <cite id="069ef15a-4">This paper describes COVID-19-related disruptions of ARV provision, and #EAWA's strategies to maintain uninterrupted ARV access during COVID-19 in both</cite> <cite id="0512daff-5">Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, CCP is delivering antiretroviral medication directly to the homes of people living with HIV in Cote d'Ivoire</cite>
- Countries exemplars: Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, Nigeria, Côte d’Ivoire, and countries across West/Central Africa coordinated by EAWA; European Union/European Economic Area systems layered telehealth and delivery-and-collect models atop home-based care infrastructures; and USA-supported programs in sub-Saharan Africa adapted pediatric and adult ART access to include remote/intermediary services.<cite id="069ef15a-4">This paper describes COVID-19-related disruptions of ARV provision, and #EAWA's strategies to maintain uninterrupted ARV access during COVID-19 in both</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-7">Arrangements were made in some countries to administer antiretroviral therapy (ART) through delivery and collection services for those unable to travel or</cite> <cite id="0512daff-5">Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, CCP is delivering antiretroviral medication directly to the homes of people living with HIV in Cote d'Ivoire</cite> <cite id="069ef15a-6">Effects of the COVID-19 Pandemic on HIV Services</cite>

Key constraints and how they were addressed
- Movement restrictions and clinic overcrowding: Delivery-and-collect, home-based ART, and telehealth reduced nonessential in-person contacts and logistical barriers, preserving continuity while managing COVID risk in facilities and communities.<cite id="069ef15a-4">This paper describes COVID-19-related disruptions of ARV provision, and #EAWA's strategies to maintain uninterrupted ARV access during COVID-19 in both</cite> <cite id="0512daff-4">Implementing telemedicine allows for maintenance of social distancing and limits in-person interactions, necessary during the COVID-19 Pandemic</cite>
- Supply chain and adherence: MCD was operationalized by adapting refill intervals, using trusted community and case manager links, and integrating adherence monitoring; regional guidance emphasized formalizing these approaches into national policy to sustain uptake beyond emergencies.<cite id="ed98fdaa-2">National programmes in 8 out of 10 countries in the region have issued guidelines for MMD of ARV drugs and take-away doses of OST drugs, beefing up their ARV</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-0">This report describes how HIV programs in Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, and Nigeria supported treatment continuation by introducing home delivery of ARVs</cite>

Bottom line
Home delivery of ART was widely accepted and implemented across Southeast Asia, large swaths of sub-Saharan Africa (via national programs, regional associations, and NGO-bilateral initiatives), and parts of Europe/Central Asia, often in combination with telehealth and delivery-and-collect models, to protect continuity of HIV treatment during COVID-19; country case studies from Indonesia, Côte d’Ivoire, and West/Central Africa exemplify rapid scale-up and patient acceptance as essential to preventing treatment interruption and associated mortality.<cite id="ed98fdaa-0">This report describes how HIV programs in Indonesia, Laos, Nepal, and Nigeria supported treatment continuation by introducing home delivery of ARVs</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-2">National programmes in 8 out of 10 countries in the region have issued guidelines for MMD of ARV drugs and take-away doses of OST drugs, beefing up their ARV</cite> <cite id="ed98fdaa-7">Arrangements were made in some countries to administer antiretroviral therapy (ART) through delivery and collection services for those unable to travel or</cite> <cite id="069ef15a-4">This paper describes COVID-19-related disruptions of ARV provision, and #EAWA's strategies to maintain uninterrupted ARV access during COVID-19 in both</cite> <cite id="0512daff-5">Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, CCP is delivering antiretroviral medication directly to the homes of people living with HIV in Cote d'Ivoire</cite> <cite id="069ef15a-2">The cost of inaction: COVID-19-related service disruptions could cause hundreds of thousands of extra deaths from HIV.
